Josh Crickmay - A Big Life

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How reconnecting with nature saved a young man's life

Unique Selling Point:
We travel to the Drakensberg in search of it's unique wildlife with a young man, who says he has nature to thank for his life... and he's now paying her back in the only way he knows... by raising awareness and passing on his knowledge to the next generation.

Summary:
His name is Josh Crickmay, a 20-something inspirational conservationist and wildlife filmmaker…
10 years ago Josh was hospitalised with severe depression. He dropped out of school. He was suicidal. Diagnosed with Aspergers, life felt overwhelming.
His parents realised he needed a massive intervention to change the course of his life. They quit their jobs and took him on a Birding Big Year… 365 days to spot 1000 different bird species.
Their travels took them across South Africa, even as far as Equatorial Guinea where they spent a month with a wildlife photographer…
When he came home, Josh was a changed person. For him, nature and his experiences within it, gave him his life back and he decided to give back, the only way he knew how…

Further information:
Josh joined the rangers at Hluhluwe, learning about wildlife and the veld. He wrote a book about his adventurous year and with the little proceeds, he started buying camera equipment… determined to tell nature’s stories, to help people understand wildlife and the importance of conserving ecosystems. His first project, called City Beasts, is a self-funded docu-series on the wildlife in and around Cape Town. From the elusive Table Mountain ghost frog, to porcupines nesting in suburbia, and the shy clawless otter. Josh sought them out to tell their stories in a unique, entertaining and humorous way.

But this is only the beginning. His dream of following in the footsteps of Attenborough and Irwin is becoming a reality. He is working on a whole array of different ideas…

City Beasts will air on People’s Weather in November this year. This is Josh’s very first proper production for broadcast. Filmed and edited by himself. A passion project. And while this is in essence a “competing channel”, they have a small viewership and it is part of the DSTV bouquet. He is not making money out of it, and his determination, love of the world, and sense of humour is inspirational!

Extra Budget Items:
3 Nights' Accommodation in Drakensberg
Travel to Amphitheatre and back
2 Additional Presenter Days (Travel days)

Other Footage Sources:
Clips from Josh about his travels

JOSH’S BIG LIFE – SCRIPT


UPSOUND
My name is Josh Crickmay – wildlife filmmaker and conservationist…


V/O
An extraordinary journey brought him back from the brink of death and gave him a sense of purpose… and humour…

This is the story of Josh Crickmay’s big life…
Drakensberg


LINK
There’s no denying it… nature feeds the soul, we draw energy from it, it’s restorative, but the experience is different for everyone… But I don’t want you to take my word for it…. There’s an adventurer who says that nature saved his life…
Josh & Claire
Claire: What is it about this area that you feel makes it special? Is it the scenery?

Josh: Yeah. Yeah. I was going to say, You mean aside from that, I mean. When we're standing here, we're looking up at those mountains. You’re thinking, that looks beautiful. But for me, I see an adventure into that to go and find something and I love the whole experience that goes into finding it as well. The challenge, the time spent out there, the beautiful things that you don't expect along the way.


Josh & Claire
Claire: Your eyes light up when you talk about this place and about nature. Josh as a young boy, five years old, did he always love nature?

Joah: Much to my parents' detriment.. Yes, way too much. It's always been the biggest part of who I am.
UPSOUND
It looks just like a leaf.

Yes.

And look at this giant cricket that I found…


Kathy
Just naturally chased bugs… that’s what he did. On the cricket field, they’d find him up a tree.
V/O
Josh grew up in a leafy Pietermaritzburg suburb, with his doting parents, Kathy and Andrew Crickmay…
Andrew
He was just lots of fun. There was always something happening with Josh. … chasing chameleons and… but he was always different.
UPSOUND
Take a picture…
V/O
But in 2012 Josh turned 15, and almost overnight, the cheerful, carefree little boy was gone…
JOsh
It started with me really, really not working well in school because I was this, this kid bent on diving into bushes after skinks. And, you know, it didn't mesh in the school system. And I got completely just crushed by that.
V/O
Josh found himself in a world where nothing made sense anymore and with each passing day he slipped deeper and deeper into a severe depression.
Kathy
You know, Josh's whole message at that time was, I can't do school because the classroom had become unbearable, so I can't do life.. So what's the point? I can't make a living for myself…. So what is the point?


Josh
I eventually got I refused to go to school and became a bit violent about if it if I was tried to be forced. And at that point my mental health began to deteriorate. And I yeah, I mean, as I said, I rotted, I rotted away.


Andrew
I was brought up, you know, you go to school, you go to university, You you know, you work hard. And when Josh woke up one day and said, listen, I'm not going to school, it was like it was like waving a red flag at a bull.

So, you know, there was a lot of conflict in that whole period because it manifested as belligerence and laziness that it wasn't… I didn't know that what I was looking at was not what I was seeing.
V/O
After being hospitalised on several occasions Josh eventually ended up on suicide watch…
Kathy

We were living literally hour by hour at times

As a parent, it's the most terrifying to watch a kid struggling and building with the struggles and building with a lot of anger and aggression and frustration or coming out of a place of fear.
V/O
It took almost a year before the family finally understood what was at the root of Josh’s overwhelming anxiety and depression…
Josh
I was diagnosed with with Asperger's or high functioning autism. And I think that was probably the main one. There was a bit of a sort of confused diagnosis of OCD you threw in quite entirely. Sure there was a bit of Asperger's. Usually comes with a mix of things.

Now it's almost like my brain uses a different algorithm. It's almost as if, I don't know if you ever stood too close to a TV screen, you get too close, and then suddenly the big picture disappears and all you can see all the pixels.


V/O
After 18 months of darkness, Kathy and Andrew realised they needed a drastic intervention.
Andrew
And funny enough, I was a little person who had a change. You know, I had to come to terms with my own worldview and then we could start to heal Josh.



Kathy
And and that's where this the big year sprung into life, which is basically a big year where you run around and chase birds for a year and try and tick off as many birds as you can in a year. And that's what we did. We got me, the girl from Umhlanga became a camper
V/O
The Crickmays set off on an adventure, hoping to reignite the spark in their son…
Josh
Our challenge was to find a thousand species of birds in within a calendar year. And we did that within southern Africa and Ecuador, deserts to the jungles. And I think because we had that goal in mind when we did fall, we were able to get back up again.


V/O
By the end of their adventure, they had recorded and photographed over 1000 birds… and Josh was a changed person, on a very different path….

He trained as a game ranger and published a book about his incredible journey…
Josh & Claire
Claire: When you first saw it, when it was bound, when the cover was chosen…

Joah: Yeah.

When everything is done. How does this feel? Like, when you look at it, does it feel like the triumph that I see?
Josh: Writing this book helped me realize that the difficulties that I went through were not the worst thing that ever happened to me, but in fact the best. It was that, it was that realization that those trials put me in the absolute right direction. I don't know where I would have been if I'd finished school and tried to do things normally. It probably would have broken me anyway,


V/O
From photography, graphic design and publishing to wildlife filmmaking… Today Josh spends most of his time with a camera in hand, in search of adventures and unique stories to tell…
Josh
It’s part of the charm… This is clunk from the Land Rover. A good Land Rover should be named after something that it does. And this one every now and again goes clunk…. And you don’t ask questions…
UPSOUND


V/O
A short walk in the Berg isn’t a typical Josh-adventure… but this doesn’t temper his excitement…
Josh
Now we’re beginning to see those mountains… the cliffs are beginning to show their faces. There’s one on the other side of this little hill, we’ll start seeing… It was brought here straight from the set of King Kong and it looks great. Nice addition!
Josh & Claire
Claire: Have you had any brushes where you thought, wow… okay, this is a dangerous situation or a close call?

Josh: There were a few. I think the Seal Island one was one… There’s a seal colony off Hout Bay and I swam to it and I had a bit of a sketchy situation…

And then I’ve had some close calls with Hyenas. I woke to some sounds and a very bad smell and it was breathing on my face… And I did what any sensible human being would do and I hit it with my pillow…

Claire: JOSH!




Danger, adventure and comedy are all ingredients in Josh’s recipe for compelling filmmaking. And with his very first TV series to be broadcast early next year, this young man’s future is filled with promise.
Kathy
What's been beautiful is watching him evolve as each door was opened and each skill is learned and each one is built on the next that he's he's just made for what he's doing right now.
Andrew
He's got a vision and he's got a dream of, of, of a certain style of, of filmmaking. And I'd just love to see him succeed at it and I'd love to see him with his own family and his own kids because I can't think of a better father. You know? I think he's going to be a great dad.
Josh
Claire: Do you feel like you are living your purpose?

Joah: Everything that has led me to this point has put me in this in this direction. And I couldn't be doing anything else. I feel that I was brought back from from the edge by by the beauty and and fascination of of this world and just what it did for me. And everything going from this point is me repaying the life debt that I owe to nature and everything that I do from this point is through to to equalize that and to give back for the extra days that it gave me.






PROMO 1 21”
An out-of-the box approach to bring their son back from the brink of death…

UPSOUND We were living literally hour by hour…

Josh Crickmay is living a big adventure, repaying a life-debt to mother nature…
PROMO 2 21”
From swimming in shark-infested waters to close encounters with hyenas…

Breathing sensible…

A young man who says that nature saved his life.
PROMO 3 21”
Just 10 years ago Josh Crickmay was enveloped in darkness, unable to imagine a future…

I rotted…

But an extraordinary journey brought him back from the brink of death, giving him a purpose and a unique place in the world.

metadata.Further information: Josh joined the rangers at Hluhluwe, learning about wildlife and the veld. He wrote a book about his adventurous year and with the little proceeds, he started buying camera equipment… determined to tell nature’s stories, to help people understand wildlife and the importance of conserving ecosystems. His first project, called City Beasts, is a self-funded docu-series on the wildlife in and around Cape Town. From the elusive Table Mountain ghost frog, to porcupines nesting in suburbia, and the shy clawless otter. Josh sought them out to tell their stories in a unique, entertaining and humorous way. But this is only the beginning. His dream of following in the footsteps of Attenborough and Irwin is becoming a reality. He is working on a whole array of different ideas… City Beasts will air on People’s Weather in November this year. This is Josh’s very first proper production for broadcast. Filmed and edited by himself. A passion project. And while this is in essence a “competing channel”, they have a small viewership and it is part of the DSTV bouquet. He is not making money out of it, and his determination, love of the world, and sense of humour is inspirational!
